patch.objective: Differentiate acute hemolytic, febrile non-hemolytic, allergic and anaphylactic reactions, TRALI and TACO by their signs and timing
secondaryObjectives: Verify blood products before transfusion, monitor most closely in the first 15 minutes, and stop the transfusion at once if a reaction is suspected

sources.cite: Australian Red Cross Lifeblood. Management of suspected reactions (clinical practice guidance)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEXRN case post-op-transfusion-reaction, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11: 'Stop the transfusion immediately and activate emergency procedures if required'; check ABC and vital signs; 'Maintain intravenous (IV) access (do not flush the existing line and use a new IV line if required)'; 'Repeat all clerical and identity checks'; 'Notify your Medical Officer and Transfusion Service Provider'; send fresh blood and urine samples with the used pack and IV line if asked; document and report; dyspnea or hypotension reactions 'Within 15 minutes of starting transfusion but may be later'; for suspected acute hemolysis maintain blood pressure and urine output.

Relayed from the NCLEXRN case post-op-transfusion-reaction, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11: fever and chills 'can also be the first sign of a more serious acute hemolytic reaction'; hypotension and red urine (hemoglobinuria) point to a more serious reaction; complications include DIC and renal failure; when a reaction is suspected 'the transfusion should be immediately stopped' with the line kept open with 0.9% saline; vital signs 'typically recorded at 15-minute intervals'.
